In [[mathematics]], in the field of [[homological algebra]], given an [[abelian category]] 
<math>\mathcal{C}</math> having enough injectives and an additive (covariant) [[functor]] 

:<math>F :\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}</math>,

an '''acyclic object''' with respect to <math>F</math>, or simply an <math>F</math>-acyclic object, is an object <math>A</math> in <math>\mathcal{C}</math> such that

:<math> {\rm R}^i F (A) = 0 \,\!</math> for all <math> i>0 \,\!</math>,

where <math>{\rm R}^i F</math> are the [[derived functor|right derived functors]] of 
<math>F</math>.<ref>{{cite book | last=Caenepeel | first=Stefaan | title=Brauer groups, Hopf algebras and Galois theory | zbl=0898.16001 | series=Monographs in Mathematics | volume=4 | location=Dordrecht | publisher=Kluwer Academic Publishers | year=1998 | isbn=1-4020-0346-3 | page=454 }}</ref>
